item.title: Urgent: Dislodged Utility Cover on Footway – Safety Hazard & Driveway Access Blocked, 8th August
item.description:
I am writing to report a dislodged utility/manhole cover on the footway/verge outside my property, which is causing both a safety hazard and an access problem. The cover has come loose from its frame and is currently sitting off to the side, leaving the chamber opening partly exposed. As it is not properly seated, it is unstable to walk or drive over, and I need to cross this section to access my driveway. Because it is loose, driving over it is dangerous, and it also poses a serious risk to pedestrians, particularly the children who regularly cycle and scooter along this stretch of pavement. Could this please be inspected and repaired or re-secured as a matter of urgency? I am happy to provide photographs showing the exact location and condition of the cover if that would help. Please let me know if you require any further information, or if this needs to be redirected to the relevant utility company responsible for this chamber. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 30, Clarendon Green, St Paul's Cray, Orpington, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: The regulatory parking restriction sign for the loading bay, 8th August
item.description:
The regulatory parking restriction sign for the loading bay at this location has been completely defaced, spray-painted, and wrapped in black material, entirely obscuring the operational hours. This has created a highly misleading and non-compliant road layout. Civil Enforcement Officers are actively exploiting this hidden sign to issue predatory parking tickets to motorists. As the Highway Authority, please inspect, uncover, or replace this sign immediately to comply with the Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions (TSRGD).

Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Road works at footscray, 7th August
item.description:
The roadworks at Footscray by Thames water are causing sidcup to come to a stand still ! They have already taken over Chislehurst Road for long term works ( into 2027) and now they've started works at these traffic lights ! It took me half an hour to get from the top of Sidcup hill to the bottom - a journey that would normally take 10 minutes ! I am a frequent visitor to this area and was unaware of any water issues ( I'm usually the one that reports them!)
